findings.title: The "partial month" test does not exercise rounding
findings.explanation: 3000 over 30 days with 20 days remaining gives exactly 2000, so this test never hits a fractional-cent result. Add a case where the amount does not divide evenly, such as 1000 cents with 10 days elapsed of 30. That case would pin down the rounding rule (round, floor or ceil) and show whether the function returns an integer. Also, 3000 * (20/30) in floating point only happens to come out at exactly 2000. If the implementation computes it that way, the assertion is fragile, so consider asserting the integer-cent behavior explicitly.

findings.title: Missing edge cases for invalid periods and other boundaries
findings.explanation: The PR claims to cover edge cases, but it does not test a zero-length or inverted period (end <= start), which would divide by zero or give a negative or NaN result. It also skips a zero amount, a 28/29-day February or 31-day month (the existing tests only use a 30-day period), and a cancellation partway through a day. Add tests that define the expected behavior, such as throwing or returning 0, for the invalid period at least.

findings.title: Duplicated start/end setup across tests
findings.explanation: The same start and end dates are repeated in every test. Hoisting them into shared constants in the describe block, or using it.each for the boundary cases, would cut the repetition and make the expectations easier to read.

findings.title: Test name says "two thirds" but the point is days elapsed
findings.explanation: The title is correct but hard-codes the fraction. A name like 'prorates by remaining days in a 30-day period' states the intent better. It would also avoid confusion with the existing half-period test, which uses the same 30-day setup.

## Add edge-case tests for proration

Covers cancellations at the start and end of a period, before it starts, after it ends, and a partial month.

@@ -19,4 +19,24 @@ describe('proratedAmount', () => {
     const end = new Date('2026-05-01T00:00:00Z')
     expect(proratedAmount(3000, start, end, new Date('2026-04-16T00:00:00Z'))).toBe(1500)
   })

+    const start = new Date('2026-04-01T00:00:00Z')

+  })
+
+  it('refunds nothing when cancelled at or after the end', () => {

+    const end = new Date('2026-05-01T00:00:00Z')
+    expect(proratedAmount(3000, start, end, end)).toBe(0)
+    expect(proratedAmount(3000, start, end, new Date('2026-05-09T00:00:00Z'))).toBe(0)
+  })
+
+  it('refunds two thirds after ten days of a thirty-day period', () => {
+    const start = new Date('2026-04-01T00:00:00Z')
+    const end = new Date('2026-05-01T00:00:00Z')
+    expect(proratedAmount(3000, start, end, new Date('2026-04-11T00:00:00Z'))).toBe(2000)
+  })
 })
